newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia-Japan PGM talks set for June 1-11 in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Russia-Japan PGM talks set for June 1-11 in Tokyo.

text.p: Japan and Russia will hold long-delayed talks on the export of platinum group metals (PGM) for 1997 from June 1-11 in Tokyo, a Russian trade official in Tokyo and Japanese traders said on Wednesday.
"We are at the final stage. PGM shipments to Japan are expected to start in late May or June," the Russian trade official said.
Japanese traders also said they had been informed by the Russian platinum group metals export agency, Almazjuvelirexport, that 1997 contract talks would take place from June 1 to 11.

The Russian official declined to comment as to whether the agency had enough supplies to meet export demand. But last week Russia assured Japanese clients that the agency could export the same volume of PGM as in 1996, traders said.

Talks between Japan and Russia on annual PGM export contracts usually take place in mid-December, but have been delayed because of Russian internal problems such as a delay in passing the 1997 federal budget and a cabinet reshuffle.
Russia supplies more than 60 percent of the world's palladium, while Japan is the world's largest consumer of PGMs, which include palladium and platinum.
